chapter: Rose Murphy, wartime 52nd Street, Town Hall
title: The war years: 52nd Street and musicians talking about the war
summary: Stewart remembers 52nd Street and the whole country hungry for jazz in 1941-45; musicians discussed the war and Slim was drafted.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years
story.community_name: Drafted: service bands, USO shows and the war years

blocks.x: Well, how do you remember the war years? How did they stack up (inaudible)? What do you recall about them?
Well, the war years were -- that was between --

'41 and '45. Well, like, if I remember, I spent a lot of time on 52nd Street and somehow, well, 52nd Street was the most prominent thing in my memory. The activity in music was terrific, you know. 52nd Street was really jumping; and, of course, when I traveled with my own group and with Art Tatum during those war years, it seemed like the whole country was eager to hear more jazz and more music, you know? Things were really popping.
How did the -- did the musicians talk much about the war, about like Mussolini and Hitler and the Japanese and stuff like that? Did the guys talk much about what

Well, yes, they did. And of course, quite a few musicians, like I mentioned my old partner, Slim Gaillard, he was inducted into the Army and the war was quite a subject amongst the musicians. They would talk about it. Some of them had to go do their turn too, you know. Of course, one thing that happened to a few musicians who had to go into the Service, where they had a chance to play their music while in the Service, you know, and that was a good thing, I thought. I never did make the Service, but that's the way it was happening.
